metadata.description: Quantitative kinetic parameter database for ExposoGraph metabolic flux modeling. All parameters derived from published literature. Confidence flags: high (multiple concordant studies), moderate (single study or derived), low (estimated from related substrates), estimated (extrapolated or inferred).

units.CLint: varies — ratio of Vmax/Km in same units

PAH.description: Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons — require metabolic activation to reactive diol-epoxide intermediates

CYP1A1.notes: Primary activation enzyme; extremely high affinity (very low Km)

CYP1B1.notes: Vmax approximate (~5.0); lower efficiency than CYP1A1

EPHX1.notes: Required intermediate step toward ultimate carcinogen BPDE; Vmax in nmol/min/mg microsomal protein

GSTM1.notes: GSTM1-null (gene deletion) = zero activity. ~25-fold increase for (-)-anti-DBPDE substrate. GST P1-1 data applied.

GSTP1.notes: Higher CLint than GSTM1 due to lower Km; expressed in lung

Aflatoxin.description: Mycotoxin requiring CYP-mediated epoxidation to the reactive AFB1-8,9-epoxide (AFBO); AFQ1 is a detoxification product

CYP3A4.notes: Hill kinetics (n≈2, cooperative). ISEF-corrected. CYP3A4 contributes ~45% of total AFB1 metabolism in HLM.

CYP1A2.notes: Michaelis-Menten. ISEF-corrected. CYP1A2 contributes ~49% of total AFB1 metabolism in HLM. Also: Gallagher 1994 values Km=41μM, Vmax=2.63 nmol/min/nmol — consistent.

CYP3A4_AFQ1.notes: Km is average of 140-180 μM affinity range; ~67 total turnover estimate

GSTA1.notes: GSTA1 is the main AFB1-epoxide conjugating enzyme in human liver; exact human Km is not well-established — estimate from rat/human comparison

Aldehyde.description: Ethanol oxidized sequentially: ethanol → acetaldehyde (ADH) → acetate (ALDH2/ALDH1A1). Acetaldehyde is the proximate carcinogen.

ADH1B_star2.genotype_label: fast metabolizer (β2β2); high Vmax but very high Km — generates more AcH at drinking concentrations

ALDH2_star1.genotype_label: wildtype — extremely high affinity and activity

ALDH2_star2_homozygous.genotype_label: variant homozygous — ~800-fold reduction in CLint vs wildtype

ALDH2_star1_star2.genotype_label: heterozygote — partial dominance model; retains ~25% of homozygous wildtype activity
ALDH2_star1_star2.notes: ALDH2*2 is dominant-negative; heterozygote retains only ~25% wildtype CLint

ALDH1A1.genotype_label: backup enzyme — lower affinity than ALDH2*1 but expressed ubiquitously

ADH5.notes: ADH5 (GSNO reductase/FDH) handles formaldehyde; quantitative human kinetics sparse

epidemiological_validation.note: 800-fold CLint reduction in *2/*2; heterozygote ~25% wildtype — consistent with dose-response OR pattern

Nitrosamine.description: Tobacco-specific nitrosamine. α-hydroxylation by CYP2A13 generates reactive methylating and pyridyloxobutylating species.

CYP2A13_methyl.notes: Km not separately reported for this branch; Vmax from same study

CYP2A6.reaction: NNK → α-hydroxy-NNK (much lower efficiency than CYP2A13)
CYP2A6.notes: CYP2A6 has much higher Km and ~200-fold lower Vmax/Km than CYP2A13. Numeric parameters not extracted — relative efficiency used.

carbonyl_reduction.notes: Carbonyl reduction to NNAL (4-(methylnitrosamino)-1-(3-pyridyl)-1-butanol) — major competing pathway; exact kinetics not provided

NDMA.description: Volatile nitrosamine formed endogenously and from diet/water. CYP2E1-mediated α-hydroxylation generates formaldehyde and methyldiazonium ion.

CYP2E1.notes: Range reflects studies with/without cytochrome b5. With b5: Km=22 μM, Vmax=173 pmol/min/mg. Without b5: Km=7.5 μM, Vmax=34 pmol/min/mg. Saturation at ~5 mg/kg oral dose. Used midpoint estimates here.

detoxification.note: No major enzymatic detoxification pathway identified for NDMA; clearance is primarily through activation and conjugation of formaldehyde downstream

HCA.description: Heterocyclic amine formed in cooked meat. N-hydroxylation by CYP1A2/CYP1A1/CYP1B1 generates reactive N-OH-PhIP.

CYP1A2.notes: Major hepatic activating enzyme for PhIP
sources: Turesky et al., referenced in PMC1829392

CYP1A1.notes: 2.75× higher catalytic efficiency than CYP1A2 due to very low Km. Extrahepatic significance.

CYP1B1.notes: Very low Vmax despite low Km → 80-fold lower efficiency than CYP1A1. Produces both N-OH (activation) and 4-OH (detox) products.

SULT1A1.reaction: N-OH-PhIP → N-sulfonyloxy-PhIP (further activation) OR competing detox sulfation
SULT1A1.notes: Sulfotransferases can both activate (N-O-sulfonylation) and detoxify N-OH-PhIP depending on tissue context; numerical kinetics not well established for human enzymes

NAT2.notes: NAT2 genotype modulates PhIP carcinogenicity — slow acetylators may have altered risk

Benzene.description: Industrial/environmental chemical. CYP2E1-mediated oxidation to phenol, then further to catechol and benzoquinone — reactive hematotoxic/leukemogenic metabolites.

CYP2E1_liver.notes: CYP2E1 responsible for ~50% of phenol metabolism at 20 μM substrate concentration. Km range 50-100 μM; midpoint used.

CYP2F2_lung.notes: CYP2F2 is significant in pulmonary microsomes; human-specific lung metabolism. Quantitative Km not extracted.

NQO1.notes: NQO1 (NAD(P)H quinone oxidoreductase) reduces benzoquinone to less reactive hydroquinone. NQO1*2 null variant associated with increased benzene toxicity. Quantitative kinetics not in provided data.

GSTT1.notes: GSTT1-null associated with benzene hematotoxicity. Quantitative kinetics not provided.

HeavyMetal.description: Heavy metals including arsenic, cadmium, chromium. Mechanism involves indirect genotoxicity — oxidative stress, DNA repair inhibition, epigenetic dysregulation rather than direct enzyme-mediated metabolism. Limited Michaelis-Menten parameters available.

AS3MT.reaction: Inorganic arsenic → methylarsonate (MMA) → dimethylarsinate (DMA) — methylation series
AS3MT.notes: AS3MT (arsenic methyltransferase) kinetics estimated from rodent and limited human data. DMA generally less toxic than inorganic arsenic.

general_ROS.reaction: Arsenic → ROS generation → oxidative DNA damage
general_ROS.notes: No Michaelis-Menten parameters applicable. Risk modeled via indirect genotoxicity score.

cadmium.reaction: Cadmium → metallothionein binding (protective) or mitochondrial/DNA damage
cadmium.notes: Metallothionein induction protects at low doses; overwhelmed at higher exposures. No standard enzyme kinetics apply.

HeavyMetal.notes: Heavy metal carcinogenicity modeling is semi-quantitative. Enzyme kinetics not applicable to primary mechanism. Use oxidative stress / DNA repair inhibition scores as proxies.

Dioxin.description: Persistent organic pollutant acting through AhR signaling rather than direct metabolic activation. Induces CYP1A1/CYP1B1 expression, amplifying downstream PAH activation.

AhR_binding.notes: Receptor-mediated mechanism. Very high potency (Kd ~0.1 nM). TEF (toxic equivalency factor) = 1.0 by definition.

Dioxin.notes: Quantitative enzyme kinetics not applicable. Model via AhR-mediated induction amplifying PAH pathway fluxes. TEF approach recommended for dioxin-like compounds.

ChlorinatedSolvent.description: TCE oxidized by CYP2E1/CYP1A2 to trichloroethylene oxide → trichloroacetaldehyde → trichloroacetic acid and other metabolites. Also conjugated to GSH via GSTT1.

CYP2E1_TCE.notes: Km estimated from TCE oxidation in human liver microsomes; Vmax data limited. CYP2E1 is primary enzyme.

GSTT1_TCE.notes: GSTT1-mediated pathway generates nephrotoxic/genotoxic metabolites (S-dichlorovinyl-L-cysteine). GSTT1-null may be paradoxically protective.

ChlorinatedSolvent.notes: TCE kinetics are reasonably understood in animal models; human-specific quantitative parameters are limited. Confidence low for quantitative flux.

genotype_modifiers.description: Scaling factors applied to Vmax for each metabolizer phenotype class. Special cases override the standard scale.

ALDH2_star1_star2.note: ALDH2*2 is dominant-negative; heterozygote retains only ~25% of *1/*1 activity

GSTM1_null.note: GSTM1-null is a complete gene deletion polymorphism (~50% population frequency)

GSTT1_null.note: GSTT1-null is a complete gene deletion polymorphism (~20% population frequency)

tissue_expression_weights.description: Relative enzyme expression levels by tissue (1.0 = high/reference expression, scaled 0-1). Based on GTEx and microsomal protein data.
